capabilities.name: CAP_CHOWN
capabilities.reason: give each jail's files to the sandbox's own uid and gid

capabilities.name: CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE
capabilities.reason: the jailer chowns the chroot root to the sandbox uid (0700) and then creates /dev and the other directories inside it; root without this is refused there (real-root runs 44348324152 failed on the pinned set without it, 44348802212 passed with it). The helper holds it in the permitted and inheritable sets only and drops it from the effective set at start-up; it is raised into the ambient set in the jailer child between fork and exec

capabilities.name: CAP_SETGID
capabilities.reason: the jailer switches to the sandbox's gid before it execs Firecracker

capabilities.name: CAP_SETUID
capabilities.reason: the jailer switches to the sandbox's uid before it execs Firecracker

capabilities.name: CAP_SYS_ADMIN
capabilities.reason: the jailer's mount namespace, bind mounts and pivot_root

capabilities.name: CAP_MKNOD
capabilities.reason: the jailer creates the device node for /dev/kvm inside the jail

notes: DeviceAllow: the jailer mknods /dev/kvm, /dev/net/tun and (when the host lists userfaultfd in /proc/misc) /dev/userfaultfd inside each jail, and it fails the launch if one mknod is refused, so each needs m. The VMM opens only /dev/kvm (rw). tun and userfaultfd get m alone: no guest NIC exists and no snapshot is restored through userfaultfd, so nothing may open them. /dev/urandom is in systemd's closed-policy default list.

Delegate=yes: the unit owns its cgroup subtree. The helper moves itself into a leaf of it at start and the jailer's cgroups sit under the unit's vms subtree, so the device policy above covers the VMM.

CAP_SYS_CHROOT is absent on purpose: the jailer enters the jail with pivot_root (covered by CAP_SYS_ADMIN), not chroot(2). The jailer source (v1.16) calls pivot_root, never chroot(2); the real-root run under this capability set confirms it.

CAP_KILL and CAP_FOWNER are absent on purpose. The helper is designed to this set: it stops a sandbox by writing cgroup.kill (kernel 5.14 or later), sets a file's mode before it chowns it, and takes each directory of a sandbox-owned tree back to root before it descends (chown with an empty path on an O_PATH descriptor, which needs only CAP_CHOWN), so the helper's own file operations never need CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE; that capability is for the jailer child.
Writes to cgroup files are ordinary permission checks for root on root-owned cgroupfs files and need no capability.
